summary.tldr: Requires the Health Minister to develop a national heart failure framework and report it to Parliament.
what_it_does: Creates a national framework to improve access to heart failure prevention, diagnosis, management and evaluation, and to reduce burdens on the health system.

Requires the framework to cover early detection, accurate diagnosis, patient and caregiver education, mental health supports, guideline-directed treatment, multidisciplinary care, remote monitoring and virtual visits.

Requires the framework to address care gaps in rural, remote and underserved communities, and to improve health data, including a national heart failure registry and better use of the Canadian Community Health Survey.

Requires the Minister to consult provincial governments, Indigenous governing bodies, health professionals, researchers, patients, caregivers and associations, and to hold at least one conference within 12 months.

Requires a framework report to be tabled in Parliament within 18 months and posted online within 10 days, then a follow-up report within five years on effectiveness, current diagnosis and treatment, and recommendations.
